job.title: Senior Interpretation Planner
job.description:

Salary: £43,317 - £47,694
Location: Bloomsbury (hybrid)

job.title: Policy and Public Affairs Manager
job.description:
I’m delighted to be partnering with an independent charitable foundation that funds research, generates evidence and informs policy to improve social and economic wellbeing, to appoint a Policy and Public Affairs Manager.

This is an exciting opportunity to join an established, talented team and play a key role in shaping policy and influencing decision-makers across the UK. You’ll manage a portfolio of policy and public affairs activity, ensuring it is strategically focused, grounded in robust evidence and, most importantly, delivers meaningful change in policy and practice.

Working closely with the Head of Policy and Public Affairs, you’ll help shape and deliver a proactive, responsive and impactful influencing programme, focusing on the issues and opportunities where the Foundation can make the greatest difference.

A key part of the role will be building and strengthening relationships with influential stakeholders across central and regional government, public bodies, regulators, sector organisations and the voluntary sector. You’ll also coordinate targeted communications and ensure the Foundation’s stakeholder engagement is well managed and effective.

What makes this opportunity particularly exciting is the access and influence it offers.

You’ll work with a team who are highly engaged in policy, gain exposure to Parliament and senior decision-makers, and have the opportunity to turn high-quality research and evidence into real-world policy change.The Foundation's work spans a fascinating range of areas, including older people, education, racial justice and equity, the justice system, civil justice, family and economic equality.

You and your experience:
  • You’ll have experience working in a policy environment (such as government agencies, regulators, the public sector, independent bodies or political parties), or experience influencing policy within industry, charitable or civil society organisations, think tanks or learned societies.
  • We’re particularly interested in candidates who have developed compelling policy positions and influencing strategies, with a strong focus on engaging government at all levels.
  • Confident digesting complex academic research
  • Experience or an understanding of the funding landscape, how funders operate and how they achieve impact would be advantageous, but isn’t essential.

What’s on offer?
You’ll be joining a fantastic team and a welcoming organisation that genuinely values its people.

  • Location: Clerkenwell, London (near Barbican and Farringdon stations).
  • Working pattern: Hybrid, with three days per week in the office or attending external events and two days working from home.
  • Salary: £53,000.
  • Contract: Permanent, full-time, with part-time hours also considered.

A snapshot of their benefits includes:
  • 28 days' annual leave, plus public holidays.
  • Enhanced family leave policies.
  • A warm, inclusive workplace culture, with active peer groups and social networks.
  • Genuine flexibility, with openness to part-time hours, compressed working weeks and job shares.

job.title: Director of Fundraising and Marketing
job.description:
﻿Do you want to use your fundraising or marketing and leadership expertise to make a lasting difference to the lives of children and young people? Are you ready to help an ambitious charity grow its reach, influence and impact?

This is an exciting opportunity to join The Young Lives Foundation (YLF) as its new Director of Fundraising and Marketing, leading the charity's next phase of growth.

YLF is an award-winning children's charity working across the South East of England, providing vital Advocacy, Mentoring, Befriending and Youth Programmes. At the heart of everything is a commitment to ensuring children and young people are heard, supported and empowered.

As YLF looks to the future, we're seeking an ambitious and inspiring leader who can bring together exceptional income generation expertise or creative marketing thinking and strategic vision to help take the charity to the next level. 

A new and pivotal strategic leadership role, you'll have the opportunity to shape how YLF is seen, understood and recognised, both locally and nationally. Through compelling storytelling, a strong and distinctive brand, meaningful partnerships and creative audience engagement, you'll help raise the charity's profile and extend its influence.

We are expecting to hear from either a fundraising or marcomms manager, who has a good understanding of how brand and fundraising come together - but we're not expecting you to bring both fundraising and marketing experience to the role - but a passion for both. 

Leading and inspiring a small team, you'll work closely with the CEO, Senior Leadership Team, trustees and colleagues across the organisation. You'll be joining a close-knit, collaborative charity where people genuinely care about their work and each other. YLF's values of honesty, innovation, flexibility and gratitude are central to its culture.

We're looking for someone with the vision, creativity and drive to help YLF achieve its ambitions. Could that be you?

The charity is based in Kent, and you'll need to be comfortable travelling to the Maidstone office and across the county to develop partnerships and build relationships with supporters, businesses and stakeholders. Being visible and accessible to colleagues and the Senior Leadership Team is also important.

  • Location: Maidstone, Kent
  • Working pattern: Hybrid, combining office, travel and home working
  • Contract: Permanent
  • Hours: Full-time, although part-time will be considered
  • Salary: Starting from £42,839

If you're an ambitious fundraising, comms, or marketing leader who wants to shape an organisation, build its influence and help change young lives, we'd love to hear from you!

Previous experience will have been developed in the charity or non-profit sector, but you don't need experience in both fundraising and marcomms - just an understanding of how the two work together.

You will provide strategic leadership and hands-on delivery across all communications channels, ensuring clear, consistent and impactful messaging to service members and wider stakeholders.

Working closely with senior leaders, you will set the communications direction, stabilise and enhance activity following the departure of the previous Comms Manager, and drive forward key projects and change initiatives.

* Coordinate stakeholder engagement activities, including developing tailored communications for partners, funders, and community organisations.

* Proven experience in a senior communications role, or as a Communications Manager ready to step up into Head of Communications responsibilities.
* Strong track record in strategic communications planning and execution across multiple channels.
* Demonstrable experience in digital and social media strategy, including managing websites and social platforms to drive engagement.

* Solid background in brand and reputation management within a complex stakeholder environment.
* Experience of internal communications and change communications, supporting organisational projects and programmes.
* Confident stakeholder engagement skills, with the ability to build relationships and influence at senior levels.
* Experience managing communications workloads in a fast-paced environment, delivering to deadlines and adjusting plans as needed.

Desirable skills:
* Previous experience working with or communicating to members and staff within health, social care, or charity sectors.
* Experience of leading communications through periods of organisational transition or restructuring.
* Familiarity with analytics tools to monitor and report on digital and social media performance.
* Experience in content strategy and storytelling to bring organisational impact to life across channels.
* Background in managing small communications teams or working in a stand-alone communications role.

This role can be full or part time, but a minimum of 4 days per week whose hours can be spread. The role is hybrid based, with 1 day per month in Kent and 1 day per month in London.

job.title: Chief Officer
job.description:
Could you help older people live more independent, connected and fulfilling lives?

Join Age Concern Epsom & Ewell as our next Chief Officer and help shape the future of a much-loved local charity, ensuring older people across the community can access the support, advice and connections they need to thrive.

Location: Epsom & Ewell, Surrey (office-based at The Old Town Hall, Epsom, with some home working possible)
Salary: £50,000 - £55,000 FTE (based on a 37 hour week)
Contract: Permanent, part time (32 hours per week)

About Age Concern Epsom & Ewell
Founded in 1947, Age Concern Epsom & Ewell is an independent local charity helping older people navigate later life, maintain their independence and enjoy better wellbeing. Our services include information and advice, medical transport, befriending, home visiting, IT support, DIY assistance and social activities, helping people access practical support and remain connected to their community.

Our work is delivered by nine part-time staff, supported by a dedicated volunteer network. In the past year, the quality of our services was recognised when our volunteer community was nominated for The King's Award for Voluntary Service. From helping people access information and advice, to providing companionship and transport to medical appointments, our work makes a tangible difference to everyday lives.

As we approach our 80th anniversary in 2027, demand for support is growing alongside the challenges of an ageing population. We need to strengthen our financial sustainability, review our services and resources, and adapt to changes in local government and partnership arrangements.

This is an opportunity to build on our strong community roots and long-standing relationships, ensuring the charity remains responsive, resilient and well placed to support older people for years to come.

As our next Chief Officer, you will:
  • Translate the charity’s strategy into practical plans, lead an initial organisational review and work with trustees to agree priorities, strengthen governance and build organisational resilience.
  • Oversee the charity’s day-to-day operations, finances and services, using evidence on costs, impact and community need to improve quality, efficiency and resource decisions.
  • Work with the fundraising team, legacy co-ordinator and trustees to strengthen existing income streams, develop new funding opportunities and support long-term financial sustainability.
  • Support and develop staff and volunteers, while building partnerships and raising awareness to extend the charity’s reach and ensure older people, families, funders and partners understand the support available.

Who you are
You will be a practical, thoughtful and motivated leader who combines strategic perspective with a willingness to get involved in the day-to-day running of a small charity. You will bring a warm, approachable and collaborative leadership style, with a genuine commitment to helping people and an appreciation of the personal, community-rooted nature of the charity.

You will bring:
  • Experience of leading people, services or an organisation and translating priorities into achievable plans.
  • Demonstrable experience of financial management, including budgeting, monitoring expenditure and making effective use of resources.
  • Experience of fundraising, income generation or developing funding opportunities.
  • Experience of managing or supporting staff and/or volunteers, with the ability to build an engaged and collaborative team.
  • The ability to assess organisational needs, review established practices and lead improvements and change constructively.
  • Strong communication and relationship-building skills, with the confidence to work effectively with trustees, colleagues, volunteers and external partners.
  • A genuine commitment to helping older people live independent, fulfilling and socially connected lives, alongside a responsible approach to the charity's long-term sustainability.
  • Knowledge of charity governance and the responsibilities involved in maintaining safe, well-managed services, including safeguarding and health and safety.

Experience in older people's services, advice, health, social care or community support would be desirable, as would experience of partnership working with local authorities, health services or other voluntary organisations.

Above all, you will be a self-starter who can identify what needs attention, ask the right questions and turn ideas into practical action. You will listen, build trust and bring people with you, balancing the confidence to lead with the judgement to involve others in shaping the charity's future.

job.title: Director of Partnership Development
job.description:
An exciting opportunity to shape the future of external partnerships at one of the UK's most distinctive universities, building influential relationships, driving income generation and creating opportunities for innovation, collaboration and long-term growth.

About the University of Buckingham
The University of Buckingham is a unique institution, recognised for its pioneering approach to higher education, personalised learning experience and commitment to academic excellence. As the UK's only private university with a Royal Charter, it has a proud history of innovation, including introducing the country's first accelerated two-year degree.

With ambitious plans for the future, the University is seeking to strengthen its external partnerships, expand its reach and develop new opportunities for collaboration and sustainable income generation.

The role
Reporting directly to the Vice-Chancellor, the Director of Partnership Development will provide strategic leadership in developing high-value partnerships across business, industry, government, education and philanthropy.

You will play a pivotal role in identifying new opportunities, building relationships with senior stakeholders and securing partnerships that support the University's long-term ambitions.

This is a broad, externally focused role, combining strategic business development, income generation and philanthropic fundraising with opportunities to support research, innovation and knowledge exchange.

Key responsibilities include:
  • Develop and secure high-value strategic partnerships across a range of sectors.
  • Build and maintain influential relationships with senior business leaders, funders and philanthropic supporters.
  • Identify opportunities for commercial collaboration, research, innovation and income diversification.
  • Lead the development of major philanthropic opportunities, including gifts, donations and endowments.
  • Work closely with the Vice-Chancellor and senior leadership to deliver ambitious partnership and income-generation objectives.
 
About you
We are seeking a commercially astute, highly credible and well-connected senior professional with a successful track record in strategic partnerships, business development, fundraising or external engagement.

You will bring:
  • Proven success in securing significant partnerships, collaborations or philanthropic support.
  • Strong commercial awareness, strategic thinking and financial acumen.
  • The confidence and credibility to engage and influence at Board and executive level.
  • Exceptional relationship-building, communication and negotiation skills.
  • An entrepreneurial approach, with the ability to identify opportunities and turn relationships into tangible results.

Experience in higher education would be advantageous but is not essential. We welcome applications from candidates across the commercial, public and not-for-profit sectors who can demonstrate the ability to build valuable partnerships and generate sustainable income.

Salary: Circa £80,000 per annum
Contract: Permanent

job.title: Chief Executive Officer
job.description:
**NB: This job has now expired and appears for reference only, but please get in touch if you are interested in similar positions.

Could you lead a charity with deep roots and a strong sense of community into its next chapter – creating greater opportunities for people with disabilities and/or neurodiversity to thrive?

Location: White Lodge, Chertsey, KT16 0FA (hybrid, minimum 3 days a week in the office)
Salary: circa £75,000
Contract: Permanent, full time, 37.5 hours per week

About us
White Lodge is a leading charity supporting children, young people and adults with disabilities and their families. With more than 60 years’ history, we support over 2,500 people across Surrey and beyond through specialist services and facilities in Chertsey.

White Lodge is a community as much as a service provider, built around our values of ENABLE: Equity, Nurture, Advocacy, Belonging, Language and Empathy. Our Active Plan 2025–30 sets four ambitions: Enhance accessibility and social opportunities; Champion customers' voices in health and social care; Transform local attitudes; and Strengthen its resources.

With strong systems, governance and a diversified income base, White Lodge is well placed for its next phase. The new CEO will provide continuity while bringing strategic, operational and entrepreneurial leadership to respond to a changing funding environment and pursue new opportunities, including a children's services tender.

As our next Chief Executive Officer, you will:
  • Strategy & Impact: Deliver White Lodge's strategy, translating ambitions into measurable outcomes and impact.
  • Leadership: Lead and develop a committed workforce, fostering an inclusive, accountable and values-led culture.
  • Governance & Finance: Partner with the Board to ensure strong governance, financial sustainability and effective risk management.
  • Operations: Ensure high-quality, person-centred services and effective organisational systems and performance.
  • Income & Partnerships: Diversify income and develop relationships with commissioners, funders, NHS partners and the wider community.
  • Influence & Advocacy: Champion customers' voices, strengthen White Lodge's profile and help transform attitudes towards disability.
  • Safeguarding & Compliance: Ensure high standards of safeguarding, regulatory compliance, equality and ethical leadership.

Who you are
  • A seasoned senior leader with significant experience in a complex organisation, ideally within charity, health, care or wider public services.
  • Experienced in leading substantial teams and complex services, with strong financial, operational and commercial understanding.
  • A strategic thinker with a track record of organisational change, sustainable growth and measurable outcomes.
  • Experienced in working effectively with a Board, commissioners, funders and strategic partners.
  • An emotionally intelligent, inclusive and entrepreneurial leader who builds trust, creates clarity and brings people with them.
  • A compelling communicator and ambassador, committed to equity, inclusion, dignity, safeguarding and ensuring lived experience shapes decisions.
  • Experience of disability, social care, children's services or another regulated service environment would be advantageous, as would commissioned services or significant tender experience. Previous CEO experience is desirable but not essential; exceptional Directors or Deputy CEOs ready to step up are encouraged to apply.

Why White Lodge?
  • Help create a world that is inclusive to all, regardless of ability.
  • Lead an established charity with a committed team, strong systems and strengthened governance.
  • Deliver the ambitions of the Active Plan 2025–30 and pursue new opportunities.
  • Work alongside customers, families, staff, volunteers and trustees who share White Lodge's values.
